questions.q: The product of HCF and LCM of two numbers 15 and 20 is
sol: HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers = 15 × 20 = 300.

questions.q: If α and β are the zeroes of the quadratic polynomial p(x) = ax² + bx + c, then αβ is
sol: Product of zeroes = constant term ÷ coefficient of x² = c/a.

questions.q: If sin θ = 4/5, then the value of 1 − cos²θ is
The probability of a sure event is
sol: A sure (certain) event always happens, so its probability is 1.

questions.q: The secant of the circle in the figure, is
questions.fig: A circle with centre O. Line AB touches the circle at P. CD is a chord. Line MN passes through the circle, cutting it at two points. OE is a radius.
sol: A secant is a line that cuts the circle at two points. MN does this.
AB is a tangent, CD is a chord (a segment, not a line) and OE is a radius.

questions.q: The volume of the frustum of a cone whose base radii are r₁ and r₂ and height ‘h’, is
questions.syllabusNote: The frustum of a cone is no longer in the current Class 10 syllabus.
sol: Volume of a frustum = (1/3)πh(r₁² + r₂² + r₁r₂).

questions.q: If 2, x, 26 are in Arithmetic progression, then the value of x is
sol: In an AP, the middle term is the average of its neighbours: x = (2 + 26)/2 = 14.

questions.q: If tan(90° − θ) = √3, then the value of cot θ is
questions.syllabusNote: Trigonometric ratios of complementary angles are no longer in the current Class 10 syllabus.
sol: tan(90° − θ) = cot θ, so cot θ = √3.

questions.q: In the figure, ΔADE ~ ΔABC and DE : BC = 2 : 3. Find (Area of ΔADE)/(Area of ΔABC).
questions.fig: ΔABC with D on AB and E on AC; DE is drawn across the triangle.
questions.syllabusNote: The areas-of-similar-triangles theorem is no longer in the current syllabus.
sol: The ratio of areas of similar triangles is the square of the ratio of corresponding sides.

questions.q: The radii of the base and the height of a cylinder and a cone are same. If the volume of the cylinder is 27 cubic units, then find the volume of the cone.
sol: Volume of cone = (1/3) × volume of cylinder with the same base and height = 27/3 = 9 cubic units.

questions.q: If 200 = 2ᵐ × 5ⁿ, then find the values of m and n.
Find the number of solutions of the pair of linear equations 2x − 3y + 4 = 0 and 3x + 5y + 8 = 0.
sol: a₁/a₂ = 2/3, b₁/b₂ = −3/5. These are not equal, so the lines intersect at exactly one point.

questions.q: In an Arithmetic progression, sum of the first six terms and sum of the first five terms are 78 and 55 respectively. Then find the sixth term of the progression.
Write the degree of the polynomial p(x) = x(x² + 3) + 5x² + 7.
sol: p(x) = x³ + 5x² + 3x + 7. The highest power of x is 3.

questions.q: If the value of discriminant of a quadratic equation is zero, then write the nature of roots of the quadratic equation.
sol: D = 0 means the equation has two equal real roots.

questions.q: Prove that 3 + √2 is an irrational number.
sol: Assume 3 + √2 is rational: 3 + √2 = a/b, with a, b integers and b ≠ 0.
This contradicts the fact that √2 is irrational.

questions.q:
Solve the given pair of linear equations by Elimination method:
2x + y = 8
3x − y = 7
sol: Substitute in 2x + y = 8: 6 + y = 8, so y = 2.

questions.q: Find the sum of first 20 terms of the Arithmetic progression 1, 5, 9, .... using formula.
Find the roots of the quadratic equation 2x² − 3x − 1 = 0 using quadratic formula.
Prove that (cos θ − sin θ·cos θ)/(cos θ + sin θ·cos θ) = (cosec θ − 1)/(cosec θ + 1).
sol: LHS = cos θ(1 − sin θ)/[cos θ(1 + sin θ)] = (1 − sin θ)/(1 + sin θ).
Divide numerator and denominator by sin θ: (1/sin θ − 1)/(1/sin θ + 1) = (cosec θ − 1)/(cosec θ + 1) = RHS.

questions.q: Find the coordinates of the point P and Q in the given graph and hence find the length of PQ using distance formula.
questions.fig: Graph with P at (1, 1) and Q at (5, 4), joined by a line segment.
sol: From the graph, P = (1, 1) and Q = (5, 4).

or.q: Find the coordinates of the point which divides the line segment joining the points (4, −3) and (8, 5) in the ratio 3 : 1 internally.

questions.q: A basket contains 36 mangoes. ¼th of them are rotten and others are good. If one mango is drawn at random from the basket, then find the probability of getting a good mango.
sol: Rotten mangoes = ¼ × 36 = 9, so good mangoes = 36 − 9 = 27.

questions.q: Draw a circle of radius 3.5 cm and construct a pair of tangents to the circle such that the angle between the tangents is 60°.
questions.syllabusNote: Constructions are no longer in the current Class 10 syllabus.
sol: Draw a circle with centre O and radius 3.5 cm.
The angle between the radii to the points of contact is 180° − 60° = 120°.
Draw radii OA and OB with ∠AOB = 120°.
Draw perpendiculars to OA at A and to OB at B. They meet at P.
PA and PB are the required tangents, with ∠APB = 60°.

questions.q: Divide p(x) = x³ + 3x² + 4x + 5 by g(x) = x² − x + 1 and find the quotient [q(x)] and remainder [r(x)].
questions.syllabusNote: Division of polynomials is no longer in the current Class 10 syllabus.
sol: First term of the quotient: x³ ÷ x² = x. x(x² − x + 1) = x³ − x² + x. Subtract: 4x² + 3x + 5.
Degree of 7x + 1 is less than the degree of g(x), so stop.

or.q: When the polynomial p(x) = x³ + 4x² + 5x − 2 is divided by the polynomial g(x), the quotient [q(x)] and remainder [r(x)] are x² − x + 2 and 4 respectively. Find g(x).
or.syllabusNote: Division of polynomials is no longer in the current Class 10 syllabus.
sol: By the division algorithm, p(x) = g(x) × q(x) + r(x), so g(x) = [p(x) − r(x)] ÷ q(x).
Divide by x² − x + 2: the first term is x, then 5, giving x + 5 with 8x − 16 left over.

Note: with the numbers as printed, x³ + 4x² + 5x − 6 does not divide exactly by x² − x + 2, so no polynomial g(x) fits all the given values. In the exam, writing the division-algorithm method above is the key step.

or.q:
Find the mode for the following data:
Class-interval: 1–5, 5–9, 9–13, 13–17, 17–21
Frequency: 1, 3, 7, 10, 9
sol: Modal class = 13–17 (highest frequency 10). l = 13, f₁ = 10, f₀ = 7, f₂ = 9, h = 4.

questions.q: ‘D’ is a point on the side BC of a ΔABC such that ∠ADC = ∠BAC. Then prove that AC² = BC · CD.
sol: Corresponding sides are proportional: AC/BC = CD/AC.

or.q: In the figure, ΔABC and ΔAMP are right angled triangles, right angled at B and M respectively. Then prove that CA/PA = BC/MP.
or.fig: Two right triangles ABC (right angle at B) and AMP (right angle at M) sharing the vertex A and the angle at A.
sol: Corresponding sides are proportional: CA/PA = BC/MP.

questions.q: Prove that “The lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal”.
sol: Given: circle with centre O, external point P, tangents PQ and PR touching at Q and R. To prove: PQ = PR.
In right triangles OQP and ORP: OQ = OR (radii) and OP is common.
So ΔOQP ≅ ΔORP (RHS congruence), and therefore PQ = PR (CPCT).

questions.q: In the figure area of sector AOBPA of radius ‘r’ is 231 cm² and the length of the arc APB is 22 cm. Find the radius of the sector and angle θ.
questions.fig: Sector OAPB with centre O, radii OA = OB = r, angle θ at O, and arc APB = 22 cm.
sol: Area of a sector = ½ × arc length × r, so 231 = ½ × 22 × r, giving r = 21 cm.

or.q: In the figure a rectangle ROQP is inscribed in the quadrant of a circle. If the length and breadth of the rectangle are 16 cm and 12 cm respectively, find the area of the shaded region.
or.fig: Quadrant OAB of a circle with centre O. Rectangle ROQP has O at one corner and P on the arc. The region of the quadrant outside the rectangle is shaded.
sol: OP is a radius and also the diagonal of the rectangle: r = √(16² + 12²) = √400 = 20 cm.

questions.q: Age of mother is twice the square of age of her son. After 8 years mother’s age becomes 4 years more than the thrice of age of her son. Find their present ages.
sol: Let the son’s age be x years. Mother’s age = 2x².

questions.q: In the figure, ABC is a triangle whose vertices are A(x, 10), B(2, 2) and C(12, 2). If Q(9, 6) is the mid-point of AC and area of ΔAPQ is 12 cm², then find the area of quadrilateral PBCQ.
questions.fig: Triangle ABC with P on AB and Q(9, 6) on AC, joined by segment PQ.
questions.syllabusNote: The area-of-a-triangle formula is no longer in the current Class 10 syllabus.
sol: Q is the mid-point of AC: (x + 12)/2 = 9, so x = 6 and A = (6, 10).
Area of PBCQ = area of ΔABC − area of ΔAPQ = 40 − 12 = 28 cm².

questions.q:
The ages of 100 patients admitted in a hospital are as follows. Draw a “less than type ogive” for the given data:
Age (in years): Less than 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70
Number of patients (cumulative frequency): 6, 15, 38, 46, 65, 84, 100
questions.syllabusNote: Ogives are no longer in the current Class 10 syllabus.
sol: Take upper class limits on the x-axis and cumulative frequency on the y-axis.
Join the points with a smooth free-hand curve. This is the less than type ogive.

questions.q: Construct a triangle with sides 6 cm, 8 cm and 9 cm and then construct another triangle whose sides are 2/3 of the corresponding sides of the first triangle.
questions.syllabusNote: Constructions are no longer in the current Class 10 syllabus.
sol: Draw BC = 9 cm. With B as centre draw an arc of 6 cm; with C as centre draw an arc of 8 cm. They meet at A. Join AB and AC.
Draw ray BX making an acute angle with BC on the side opposite A. Mark 3 equal points B₁, B₂, B₃ on BX.
Join B₃C. Through B₂ draw a line parallel to B₃C meeting BC at C′.
Through C′ draw a line parallel to CA meeting BA at A′.
ΔA′BC′ is the required triangle, with sides 2/3 of ΔABC.

Find the solution of the given pair of linear equations by graphical method:
2x + y = 8
x + y = 5
sol: Plot both lines. They intersect at (3, 2).

questions.q: In an Arithmetic progression the sum of first n terms is 210 and the sum of first (n − 1) terms is 171. If the first term of the Arithmetic progression is 3, then find the Arithmetic progression and find its 20th term.

or.q: The sum of interior angles of a polygon of ‘n’ sides is (n − 2) 180°. If the interior angles of a pentagon are in Arithmetic progression and its least angle is 72°, then find all the interior angles of the pentagon.
sol: Sum of interior angles of a pentagon = (5 − 2) × 180° = 540°.

questions.q: In the figure the poles AB and CD of different heights are standing vertically on a level ground. From a point P on the line joining the foots of the poles on the level ground, the angles of elevation to the tops of the poles are found to be complementary. The height of CD and the distance PD are 20√3 m and 20 m respectively. If BP is 10 m, then find the length of the pole AB and the distance AC between the tops of the poles.
questions.fig: Poles AB and CD stand on level ground with feet B and D. P lies between B and D. BP = 10 m, PD = 20 m, CD = 20√3 m.
sol: In ΔABP: tan 30° = AB/BP, so AB = 10/√3 = 10√3/3 m ≈ 5.77 m.
AP = BP/cos 30° = 20/√3 m and CP = PD/cos 60° = 40 m.

questions.q: Prove: “Basic proportionality theorem” or “Thales theorem”.
sol: Given: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC, with D on AB and E on AC. To prove: AD/DB = AE/EC.
Construction: Join BE and CD. Draw EN ⟂ AB and DM ⟂ AC.
ar(ADE)/ar(BDE) = (½ × AD × EN)/(½ × DB × EN) = AD/DB.
ar(ADE)/ar(DEC) = (½ × AE × DM)/(½ × EC × DM) = AE/EC.
ΔBDE and ΔDEC are on the same base DE and between the same parallels DE and BC, so ar(BDE) = ar(DEC).

questions.q: An insect control device made of a cylinder, a frustum of a cone and a hemisphere attached to each other is as shown in the figure. Sticky liquid is completely filled in the hemispherical part. If the radii of hemisphere and cylinder are 21 cm and 14 cm respectively and total height of the device is 60 cm and height of the cylinder is 15 cm, then calculate the curved surface area of the device and also find the quantity of the sticky liquid in the hemisphere.
questions.fig: From top to bottom: an open cylinder (radius 14 cm, height 15 cm), a frustum widening from radius 14 cm to 21 cm, and a hemisphere of radius 21 cm filled with liquid. Total height 60 cm.
questions.syllabusNote: The frustum of a cone is no longer in the current Class 10 syllabus.
sol: Height of frustum = 60 − 15 − 21 = 24 cm. Slant height l = √(24² + (21 − 14)²) = √(576 + 49) = 25 cm.
CSA of frustum = π(r₁ + r₂)l = π × 35 × 25 = 875π.
